method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer); one date helper in a small module, the rules in one module, and the claimant's and the beneficiary's questions in two seat modules importing it; one regulative rule (the three months after the grant, s 11(1)) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Testator's Family Maintenance Act 1912 (Tas), No. 7 of 1912, consolidated version published 2021-11-11 and current at point in time 2026-11-06, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-1912-007.txt (text sha256 4523ceb7dcfa509c6c7084eebe078e4ee2f295de72f52d152c2dcbcb1fb31b33), retrieved from legislation.tas.gov.au on 2026-11-06

seats: the claimant: the spouse or partner in a significant relationship, child (adopted, step- or surrogate child), parent where no spouse or child was left, or former spouse or partner receiving maintenance, who applies or for whom an application is made for provision out of the estate of a person who has died (tfm-seat.l4)
the beneficiary: a person taking under the will or intestacy whose share bears the provision, answering the claim (tfm-seat-beneficiary.l4)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run tfm-dates.l4 ; l4 run tfm-rules.l4 ; l4 run tfm-seat.l4 ; l4 run tfm-seat-beneficiary.l4 ; l4 run tfm-cases.l4 ; l4 run tfm-beneficiary-cases.l4
checks.result: 93 assertions written, 93 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics were read; satisfied assertions were counted by distinct source range. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: Focus: the provisions a claimant meets. In: ss 2(1), 2(2), 3(1)-(5), 3A, 4(2), 7(a), 8(1), 9(4), 9(5), 9(5A), 9(6), 10A(1), 10A(2), 11(1)-(4). Out: s 1 (short title); ss 2(3)-(5), 5, 8(3) (repealed or omitted); ss 4(1), 4(3), 6, 8A, 9(1), 9(2) (procedure and evidence for the Court); s 7(b) (a matter regarded, no rule); ss 8(2), 9(3), 9(7), 10, 10A(3), 10B (effects of an order and the Court's powers in framing it). Reasons in NOTES.md.
